problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & -5 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained from the columns of $A$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, find  the value of ${q}_{12}\cdot {r}_{12}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the QR Factorization of a Matrix
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093486/assets/63d523f869217b4ba3da33cb4f3524802cf5e4d545e17b75e42ab520fb281ce5.png)

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns $\mathbf{q}_1,\mathbf{q}_2$ of $Q$ were obtained from the columns of $A$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, find  the value of $q_{11} \cdot r_{12}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Let $\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2$ be the columns of $A.$

First, we find an orthonormal basis of $\textrm{Col}(A)=\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**. We set ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093486/assets/9c487a6edad04f5c2d192eab5c5cdacbcf3414cbc3c2ea556aca7fa54aec146c.png)

**Step 2**. We find the vector $\mathbf{v}_2$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{v}_1\}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-\frac{12}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we normalize $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $R\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{6} & 2\sqrt{6} \\ 0 & \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following QR factorization of $A\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093486/assets/be0eeeaf5091163ff418b9c9380a30573e27a7844548e07d8aa4eb89269f39d5.png)

Finally, $q_{11} \cdot r_{12} = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\right) \cdot \left({2\sqrt6}\right) = 2.$

feedback.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ of $A$ are orthogonal, and that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained by normalizing the columns of $A,$ what is the value of ${q}_{12}\cdot {r}_{22}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the columns of $A$ are already orthogonal, to construct an orthogonal matrix $Q,$ we simply normalize ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by ${Q}^{T},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Finally, ${q}_{12}\cdot {r}_{22}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot 2\sqrt{2}=2.$
